title: QUIC Non-HTTP/3 Interop-Testcase Inventory Verification
verification_method: Workflow review, requirement-home tests, helper dry-run plans, artifact inspection, SpecTrace validation, and Workbench validation.
preconditions: The documented upstream QUIC testcase inventory remains available from quic-interop-runner documentation.
The repository keeps the existing supported subset stable while the inventory/profile slice is drafted.
scope: Verify that the repository can represent every documented non-HTTP/3 upstream QUIC testcase as an explicit inventory/profile cell with a clear classification, while HTTP/3 stays out of scope and no broad interop-readiness claim is implied.
procedure: Review the upstream QUIC testcase documentation and confirm the documented non-HTTP/3 suite is the inventory source.
Confirm the new requirement and architecture define explicit classes for supported, intentionally unsupported, prerequisite-blocked, and non-mappable cells.
Confirm HTTP/3 remains excluded from the inventory/profile.
Confirm the helper/workflow surface can emit or plan per-cell artifact retention for the inventoried cases without silently collapsing them into generic unsupported fallthrough.
Run the requirement-home tests and helper script tests tied to the inventory/profile slice.
Run SpecTrace core validation and Workbench core validation.
expected_result: The repository has a canonical non-HTTP/3 testcase inventory/profile that makes the broader upstream QUIC suite visible and classed without widening the support promise, while HTTP/3 remains out of scope.
status_summary: The helper now accepts the documented non-HTTP/3 inventory and emits per-run inventory artifacts. The dry-run proof keeps versionnegotiation, keyupdate, and resumption green while explicitly classifying chacha20, zerortt, v2, rebind-port, rebind-addr, and connectionmigration as prerequisite-blocked. Chacha20 remains blocked pending CipherSuitesPolicy support. Zerortt remains blocked on hosted/Linux runner proof, client-side 0-RTT request-stream proof, harness classification, and first-flight key-share/HelloRetryRequest compatibility; server-role dispatch, client-side probe emission, hosted workflow wiring, resumption PSK acceptance, internal admission-gate proof, and bounded internal early-data runtime proof are not support evidence. The server-role harness path now enables managed resumption tickets plus server early-data admission for a runner-driven zerortt attempt, and the manual hosted workflow now exposes an advisory `zerortt-server-proof` profile for Linux evidence collection. A local 2026-05-09 Windows zerortt runner attempt preserved artifacts under artifacts/interop-runner/server-zerortt-quic-go/20260509-114555424-server-nginx/ but failed before Incursa execution because the upstream testcase's 250-character filenames exceeded the Windows temp-path limit. Hosted run `25608915721` on 2026-05-09 preserved explicit inventory and runner artifacts, reached managed server execution, saw quic-go install 0-RTT write keys and send 0-RTT packets on the second connection, and served one runner request stream, but failed with quic-go reporting `0-RTT was rejected` after receiving the server HelloRetryRequest required by the current P-256-only crypto floor for quic-go's hybrid/X25519 first-flight key-share offer. Resumption source-level managed-server ticket issuance and PSK acceptance are implemented under REQ-QUIC-CRT-0150 and REQ-QUIC-CRT-0151, and the harness now emits opt-in managed SSLKEYLOGFILE traffic-secret lines. A live 2026-05-09 resumption runner attempt passed with runner report artifacts/interop-runner/20260509-001723585-both-quic-go/runner-report.json recording `result: succeeded`.

supplemental_sections.heading: Deferred Coverage
supplemental_sections.content: HTTP/3 remains out of scope for this inventory/profile slice. Turning blocked or unsupported cells green is separate from making the inventory explicit. The resumption inventory cell is green only for the checked TLS session-resumption runner cell with SSLKEYLOGFILE-backed proof. The next unresolved zerortt prerequisites are hosted/Linux runner proof, client-side 0-RTT request-stream proof, harness classification, and runner first-flight key-share/HelloRetryRequest compatibility; the internal admission-gate proof, bounded internal early-data runtime proof, hosted partial-stream proof from run `25608915721`, and server-role runner dispatch are necessary but not support evidence by themselves.
